newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 29.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
- BROADMOOR DANGER MEN TO BE MOVED TO LONDON
Anger has greeted the news that patients from Broadmoor, Rampton and Ashworth top-security hospitals are to be transferred to a less secure unit in a London suburb.
- SCHRODERS TO SEVER LINKS WITH REGAN

Schroders bank is to discontinue all involvement with Andrew Regan, following Hambros' apology to the CWS over its role in the discredited entrepreneur's attempted takeover. Schroders had taken a shareholding in Regan's Lanica some months ago, and was one of the main parties in the Galileo vehicle which hoped to take over the CWS.
- SINGAPORE EYES A COM CAB PICK-UP
Executives from the Singapore Bus Service are understood to be interested in buying the Computer Cab business, which accounts for one in ten of London's cabbies.
- BOEING TARGETS CONGRESS OVER CHINA ORDERS

Boeing, the world's largest aircraft manufacturer, is leading an industry campaign to lobby the US congress to renew China's Most Favoured Nation status, in the hope of giving its proposal for 4bn dollars of aircraft orders the best possible chance in Beijing.
